title: India: Delhi chokes on most polluted Diwali eve in 10 years
summary: Delhi was ranked as the world's most polluted major city on the eve of Diwali. Delhi's air pollution is expected to get worse in the coming days. DW has more.

image.caption: Delhi residents woke up Sunday to 'very unhealthy' levels of air pollutionImage: Anushree Fadnavis/REUTERS

blocks.text: Delhi most polluted city in world on Diwali eve

blocks.caption: People in the capital woke up to a thick smog as pollution worsened in DelhiImage: Anushree Fadnavis/REUTERS

blocks.text: Delhi awoke Sunday morning enveloped in smog with poor visibility after the previous night saw the worst air quality for Diwali eve in 10 years.
The worst polluted pre-Diwali day was in 2016 when on October 29 the air quality index hit 404 on India's Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
On Saturday, the day before Diwali, Swiss ​group IQAir had ranked Delhi as the world's most polluted major city.
IQAir said Delhi had a "very unhealthy" air quality index (AQI) of 201 on Sunday.
The air quality is forecast to turn "severe" on Sunday, with Diwali celebrations adding to the pollution.

While vehicular emissions and stubble burning in neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana are major contributors to air pollution, Diwali celebrations, which involve large-scale burning of firecrackers, add to the pollution in the city.
The government had already ordered schools in and ​around Delhi to offer online classes, and ​encouraged people to work from home ahead of ⁠the Hindu festival of light.
